pairs.question: Quis precor hic toto iamdudum fervere campo quem tueor quemque ipsa vides? nam te quoque tali attonitam virtute reor.
pairs.answer: Ipsum Aesoniden cernis, soror, aequore tanto debita cognati repetit qui vellera Phrixi nec nunc laude prior generis nec sanguine quisquam.
pairs.derivation: Medea (disguised Juno frames her: 'tunc his germanam adgreditur ceu nescia dictis:' dropped as narration) asks who the raging warrior is - a genuine interrogative (quis). Juno's reply frame 'contra aspera Iuno reddit... ait' is dropped as a speech tag; kept the contiguous answering span 'ipsum ... Aesoniden cernis, soror ... sanguine quisquam.' which directly identifies the man (Aesonides/Jason seeking Phrixus's fleece). Cut at the first full stop after 'quisquam'; what follows ('aspicis ut Minyas inter...') turns to a fresh rhetorical question and elaboration, so it is excluded. First word capitalized; no Latin altered, reordered, or invented.
